breaking.headline: FAA ground-stop fallout: 4,100+ flights canceled Saturday as Duffy demands $50B overhaul
breaking.fact: More than 2,500 U.S. flights were canceled Saturday, with FlightAware's live tally climbing past 4,100 by late morning, after Friday's 4-hour nationwide ground stop wiped out 6,600+ flights; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is calling for $50 billion in emergency funding to modernize air-traffic control, and officials tied the failure to an update on an L3Harris-operated network and aging equipment. The stop, lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, was the longest nationwide halt in 25 years.

breaking.headline: Nvidia earnings Tuesday, Anthropic IPO pricing Wednesday: twin tests for the AI trade
breaking.fact: Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 results Tuesday Nov 17 under interim CEO Colette Kress, with analysts expecting about 90% earnings growth on roughly $109 billion of revenue; Anthropic prices its IPO Wednesday Nov 18 — 825 million shares at $70 to $78, targeting up to a $1.4 trillion valuation and $64.4 billion raised, trading Thursday as ANT. Nvidia's market value has fallen from about $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion.

breaking.headline: Tanker capsizes docked riverboat in New Orleans; 32 hospitalized, all aboard safe
breaking.fact: The 520-foot tanker Atlantic Asphalt lost control and struck the docked American Heritage paddlewheeler about 12:30 p.m. Friday near the Crescent City Connection bridge, capsizing it as passengers were disembarking; roughly 180 to 190 passengers and crew were aboard, all accounted for, and 32 were taken to hospitals with no critical injuries. The Coast Guard closed the river between mile markers 93 and 96 and the NTSB sent a team; a steering failure is suspected and the cause is under investigation.

breaking.headline: U.S. loses measles elimination status after 26 years
breaking.fact: A Pan American Health Organization expert panel determined the U.S. has lost the measles elimination status it held since 2000, after the same strain circulated without a break for more than 12 months; the CDC has counted 5,412 confirmed cases in 2026 across 45 states — more than double 2025's 2,289 and the highest in 35 years. To regain the status, the U.S. must go 12 months without continuous transmission.

weekInBrief.headline: IEA: oil market swings back to surplus as OPEC+ pumps more
weekInBrief.body: The International Energy Agency said Friday the oil market is expected to return to surplus in the fourth quarter, the first since the Iran war began; OPEC+ output surged 1.96 million barrels a day to 27.16 million in October, U.S. crude production hit a record 14.013 million barrels a day, and EIA inventories rose 4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million. Brent and WTI still fell about 2.5% on the week, their second straight weekly drop.

weekInBrief.headline: Dollar hits strongest since April 2025; gold slides to near one-year low
weekInBrief.body: The dollar index rose to 103.41 on Friday, its strongest since April 2025, as the euro fell to 1.1027; gold eased to $3,875.90 an ounce, holding near Thursday's one-year low, and copper fell 1.56% to $6.09, heading for a fifth straight weekly drop.

weekInBrief.headline: Fed officials push for higher rates as inflation stays hot
weekInBrief.body: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he is leaning toward a 25-basis-point hike at the December meeting and would consider 50 basis points if monthly inflation runs 0.3% or higher; Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, who dissented in October in favor of a hike, also said policy needs to become more restrictive, with October wholesale inflation running 6.5% year on year.

weekInBrief.headline: Microsoft outage spans 70+ countries, knocks out Outlook and Teams for 20 hours
weekInBrief.body: A Microsoft outage spanning more than 70 countries knocked out Outlook, Teams and Copilot for about 20 hours this week, hitting police, pharmacies and banks among others — a reminder of how much daily life runs through a single provider.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: CENTCOM on Saturday dismissed Tehran's claims that three tankers struck Iranian mines in the strait as “false” and “another example of their lies and efforts to intimidate,” after Iran's navy said a third tanker caught fire and was immobilized east of the strait and warned any tanker entering its restricted zone would face the same fate; it is the third straight day of claimed mine strikes, with Tehran claiming the incidents have disabled tankers carrying more than 4 million barrels of oil, a figure with no independent confirmation and no vessel names or flags given. On oil, Kpler's tracking still shows zero Iranian crude loadings since late August — September was the first zero month since tracking began in 2013 — and the floating storage Iran had been selling from is now drained, while at least 4.1 million barrels of Iranian LPG have slipped past the blockade on eight tankers since mid-July; non-Iranian crude keeps moving, at about 7.3 million barrels a day through the strait in the week to October 28.

space.headline: Ship 42's tower catch is hours away — after the booster waved itself off
space.body: Ship 42 is healthy in orbit after Friday's 4:47 p.m. CT liftoff from Starbase, having deployed all 26 Starlink V3 satellites, and SpaceX still plans the first-ever catch of an upper stage at the tower about 3:19 p.m. CT today, after a deorbit burn at about 2:21 p.m. CT; the booster catch already failed — Booster 22 detected a guidance and navigation problem, called off its own return, and exploded above the Gulf — and Elon Musk puts the odds of catching the ship at “more likely than not,” with three Starlink satellites carrying cameras to photograph the heat shield for the final go/no-go call.

space.headline: One CRISPR infusion kept monkeys' blood fats low for three years
space.body: A single infusion of a CRISPR gene-editing treatment kept triglycerides low in monkeys for three years, researchers at Verve Therapeutics report in Nature; the treatment disables ANGPTL3, a liver gene that slows fat clearance, cutting ANGPTL3 protein about 94% and triglycerides 43% on average, with LDL down 13%. The human version, VERVE-201, is in a phase 1b trial for people whose blood lipids stay high on medication.

space.headline: Some of the oldest rocks ever found: 3.95 billion years old
space.body: Rocks found in northern China's Shimen Complex date back 3.95 billion years, among the oldest ever discovered, researchers report in Nature; zircon-crystal dating suggests a process similar to modern plate tectonics was already under way in at least one part of Earth nearly 4 billion years ago — scientists have searched for rocks older than 3.8 billion years in China for decades.

space.headline: New trick cuts through star glare, revealing a hidden exoplanet
space.body: A Northwestern-led team built a method called FLIP that models a telescope's imperfections to erase star glare, improving the James Webb Space Telescope's sensitivity up to 15 times; applied to two-year-old observations it revealed the giant planet 51 Eridani b, hidden in plain sight, and the approach could uncover smaller, colder, fainter planets without new telescopes.

apod.title: Chandra Finds Possible Origin of 'Treble Clef' Waves
apod.credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/INAF-IRA/A. Botteon et al.; Infrared: UKIDSS-GPS; Radio: ASTRON/LOFAR; Image processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/N. Wolk
apod.explanation: A formation of radio waves looks remarkably like a treble clef in this image from NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory. Researchers used Chandra to find that the Treble Clef is likely caused by an outburst from a supermassive black hole, followed by a collision of two galaxy clusters.
